diy.b: The real cost isn't just the hours. Gaps built on assumptions in your risk assessment, program and operational documents carry straight through to your final output.

diy.b: Foundations is tailored to your business, rather than templated output that can be ineffective and difficult to defend.

software.b: A questionnaire can only ask the questions its designers anticipated. Our practitioners ask the follow-ups - how client money actually moves, who touches it, what unusual would look like in your firm - and build the assessment from what we find, not just what a form collects.

software.d: A pre-built framework applied to your sector
software.n: Tailored assessment of the firm's actual services, customers, channels, jurisdictions and operating model
software.b: No two firms in the same sector carry the same risk - a suburban conveyancer and one acting for offshore investors have little in common. A sector framework rates the average firm. We assess your actual services, clients, channels and jurisdictions, so the ratings mean something.

software.n: Policies, procedures, controls and governance designed around the business
software.b: A generated program describes a standard process, not necessarily yours. Any gap between what the documents say and what your firm actually does is exactly what an independent evaluation will find. We design the program around how you genuinely operate, so document and reality match.

software.d: No one - the output reflects whatever information you enter
software.n: A specialist tests assumptions, identifies gaps and challenges risk ratings before anything is finalised
software.b: Software treats your answers as facts: rate a risk too low going in and the platform confidently builds your entire program on the error. A practitioner's job is to catch it first - testing your assumptions is what makes the final program defensible.

software.d: You configure and implement it yourself - templated output built from your own responses, so critical substance can be missed
software.n: Approximately 35 hours committed by Nimbi's AML/CTF specialists across assessment, program, training and implementation. Your time is limited to the fact find, workshops and review
software.b: The work exists either way - the question is who carries it. Self-service means partners spending evenings configuring a platform. With Foundations, our specialists carry around 35 hours of assessment, drafting, training and implementation, and your time is limited to fact find, workshops and review.

software.n: Tailored training using the firm's roles, procedures, risks and practical scenarios
software.b: Generic modules teach definitions. Effective training teaches your people to recognise the moment a matter on their own desk becomes a red flag - so we train with your services, your client types and your escalation paths. It also makes your training records credible evidence, not a tick-box.

software.n: Templates, quick-reference guides, reporting bundle, governance responsibilities and implementation support
software.b: A program only works if the person onboarding a client on a Friday afternoon knows exactly what to do without opening a policy. We build that layer - checklists, quick-reference guides, reporting templates and a governance rhythm - so the program runs in daily practice, not just on paper.

software.d: Risk ratings build client by client as you enter them - the back book you already hold stays unmapped unless you work through it yourself
software.n: Your full client book segmented, screened and risk-rated into tiers, giving each client a review cadence and your firm a defensible ongoing monitoring baseline from day one
software.b: Ongoing CDD applies to the clients you already hold, not just the next one through the door. Working through a back book client by client is the job nobody gets to. We segment, screen and risk-rate the whole book up front, so your highest-risk existing relationships surface now - not in three years.

software.d: Your program lives inside the platform - if the subscription ends, so does the system operating it
software.n: Your program, policies and records are yours, whatever verification technology you use now or later
software.b: Generally, AML/CTF records must be kept for seven years - most software subscriptions don't last that long. If your program lives inside a platform, ending the subscription ends the system that operates it. Everything Nimbi builds sits in your own files and survives any change of technology.
